result.summary:
The cut is real work and it improved the pool, but it is INCOMPLETE and it breached the freeze once. Mechanically the pool is clean: zero em dashes, digits, semicolons, exclamation marks, contractions, first person, will/shall, or bare priest/mayor/singular elder anywhere in the NOW or unchanged text — verified by grep. 42c is the one rule finished to the end: all three archaisms ("pedlar", "drinking house" twice) survive ONLY in WAS lines and none in the delivered text. That pattern is the diagnostic — the implementer ran the sweep rule by rule and died during 42d, not at random: six faces got the speaker put into his own sentence and six identical constructions were left untouched beside them, and 42b was barely started.

ONE BLOCKING BREACH. Variant 3 face 3 [tavern · pair 1 · disagree] gained a whole new sentence that was in no WAS line: "Both sit at the same table." That is not a wording change, it is an added claim, and an added claim is outside the freeze exactly as a moved one is — the old refutation does not cover it. It is also a textbook 42a failure: delete it and the first sentence loses no fact, because it only tells the reader what to make of the memory asymmetry. Cut it.

THREE MORE CHANGED LINES NEED THE CHAIR. Variant 3 face 2 changed "what is given here" to "what they give here", which moves the AGENT from the whole place to the household heads; that is the audit's own definition of a moved claim (who is doing something), and it weakens the pair-1 disagreement, since the elders now assert only about their own giving while the tavern still asserts about everyone's. Variant 2 face 4 re-specified the tavern's speakers as "the men who take the work", a class not on the [tavern] card, and left "another does it" with a loose antecedent. Two stranger faces (V2F1 "lends him a thing", V3F1 "he learns") put the speaker in as the party acted upon; I read those as the sanctioned 42d method rather than moved claims, but all four are collected below as 42b sharpenings because the implementer left NO 42b list before it died, and each picks a reading the card must now be re-checked against.

THE POOL-GRAIN FAILURE IS SHAPE. All 20 faces are "a role says a fact" — 20 of 20, after the cut, with not one alternative shape introduced. The owner flagged four in seven as too many. Worse, the cut moved AWAY from variety (V2F4 gained an explicit "say"). The chair should see WHY: three of the five lawful alternatives are mechanically foreclosed by the freeze's own "no speaker deleted, no attribution dropped" — the bare fact, the found-thing (habitual to one-off is a moved claim), and nobody-has-done-something are all unavailable to a line editor. Only "someone DOES something" survives, where the source IS the actor, and it is free: "Those who keep the ground speak the same words over the house that gives everything and the house that gives nothing" drops no attribution at all. The implementer used it zero times. That is a brief conflict to resolve, not just an implementer failure.

THE CUT WAS CUT SHORT. Twelve of the sixteen untouched lines still fail the owner standard, including all three spines. By my count 4 of 23 lines passed before and 10 of 23 pass after — a real gain, but less than half the pool, and the twelve below are the remainder of the same pass the implementer was in the middle of.

findings.now: The heads of the households hold that what they give here is given outright.

The 42d instinct is right and the line needed a stake, but the stake was bought by narrowing the claim's scope, and that also thins pair 1: the elders now assert only about their own giving while the tavern half still asserts about all giving, so the two no longer collide head on. result.summary: The 42c half of the cut is CONFIRMED complete and correct: I greped every live line (20 NOW lines, 7 unchanged faces, 3 spines) and found zero instances of granary, infirmary, pedlar, sexton, alehouse, bier, billhook, gaol, watchman, night patrolman or factor, and zero mechanical-bar breaches (the only digit/em-dash hits are the file's own header and FACE labels; the only apostrophes are possessives — town's, trader's, hall's — not contractions). No speaker was deleted and no attribution dropped anywhere; all five source pairs still disagree or reinforce as tagged; the face-count register is untouched (9 faces per variant, tags unchanged). Several cuts are genuinely good work: V1 F3 retires "sexton" to "Whoever keeps the ground" and gains a stake with "sends him fewer"; V2 F4 folds the trailing "and that is said with some pride" back inside the sentence, which is exactly ruling 42; V1 F5 and V1 F8 add the speaker's own word ("his night round", "the trades") without touching the fact. WHERE IT FAILS IS THE FREEZE. Four faces moved their claim. Twice (V1 F6, V3 F7) a habitual practice of the town was demoted to a single thing that happened to one traveller — the audit's own named failure mode — and in V3 F7 the answering party ("the town") was also dissolved into a passive. Once (V3 F2) an entire new sentence of fact was invented: "The table can put a name to him" is not in the old line and has never been refuted. Once (V1 F2) a new ordering fact rode in, that the market hears before the hall. One further line (V2 F1) is a real 42b sharpening that must be collected and refuted — the passive "The store is kept" became "The hall keeps the store", naming a keeper the old line left open, and it now rubs against V2 F7 in the same variant where the guilds say "the keeping of the store falls on the trades". Because the implementer died before reporting, NO 42b list exists; this one line is the whole list and it was never handed over. Two structural gaps remain. The brief's VARY THE SHAPE instruction was not executed at all: all 27 faces are still "a role says a fact", and the cut pushed two lines further INTO that frame (V1 F4 from a passive to "they call", V3 F8 from a trailing attribution to a front-loaded "The guilds say"). None of the lawful alternatives — someone FOUND something, someone DOES something, the bare fact — is used on any face in the pool. And the withholding tail ("and does not say where", "and gives no reason for it", "and leaves it there", "and does not say whether it would if asked") sits on four faces, three of them in variant 3 alone. Finally the cut was cut short: four untouched faces still fail the standard (V2 F6 and V3 F4 give the speaker no stake, V2 F9 leaves "the wage" reading two ways and ends on a writer's comment, V3 F6 hides the gatekeeper behind "Whoever holds the way through"), and the V3 spine — which the implementer DID touch — still says the question "is answered one way at the hall and another at the market" without naming either answer, which is verbatim the 42b failure the brief illustrates with "The town argues about this". On the owner's own standard the pool goes from 9 of 30 lines passing to 25 of 30, a real gain carried almost entirely by the vocabulary sweep. Land it after the four freeze reversions and the V3 spine; route V2 F1 to refutation as the pool's sole 42b line.

findings.was: By a pedlar's account the way to the granary is pointed out here before the way to the inn.
findings.now: By a travelling trader's account the way to the grain store was pointed out to him before the way to the inn.
findings.why: The old line claims a HABITUAL practice of the town ("is pointed out here" — to anyone who arrives). The new line claims a ONE-OFF that happened to this trader ("was pointed out to him"). The audit's own test names habitual-to-one-off as a moved claim, and the town-wide custom is the fact the card was refuted against; a single occasion is not covered by that refutation. The 42c half of the change (pedlar to travelling trader, granary to grain store) is correct and should be kept.
findings.proposedFix: A travelling trader says the way to the grain store is pointed out to him here before the way to the inn.

findings.was: A traveller reports that the town answers a question about the granary with a question about who is asking.
findings.now: A traveller reports that his question about the grain store was answered with a question about who was asking.
findings.why: Same failure as V1 F6 and compounded. The habitual claim ("the town answers a question ... with a question") becomes one question asked once by one man, and the answering party — "the town" — is dissolved into a passive, so the line no longer says who does the deflecting. Both the frequency and the actor moved.
findings.proposedFix: A traveller reports that his questions about the grain store are answered here with a question about who is asking.

findings.was: At the tavern they say the granary is minded by the hall and opened by whoever the hall listens to.
findings.now: At the tavern they say the store is minded by the hall and opened by whoever the hall listens to. The table can put a name to him.
findings.why: A whole sentence of new fact was added. The old line deliberately leaves the man unnamed; the new one asserts that the tavern knows who he is, which is a claim about the drinkers' knowledge that appears nowhere in the old line and has never been refuted against the card. It is not a 42b cure either — it does not name him, so the vagueness it was presumably aimed at survives while an unrefuted fact rides in behind it. The pair still disagrees with FACE 1 either way.
findings.proposedFix: At the tavern they say the store is minded by the hall and opened by whoever the hall listens to.

findings.was: At the market they say the granary door opens on the word of whoever fills the store, and that the hall is told afterwards.
findings.now: At the market they say the store door opens on the word of whoever fills it, and that the hall hears of it after the market does.
findings.why: The old line orders two things: the door opens, then the hall is told. The new line orders three, inserting the market ahead of the hall in the telling. That the market learns before the hall is a new fact about who knows what when, and it is the kind of precedence claim the market has an interest in — precisely why it needs its own refutation rather than a free ride on the old one. The mildest of the four moves, since the core fact (the hall is told after the event) survives.
findings.proposedFix: The stallholders say the store door opens on the word of whoever fills it, and the hall is told after.

findings.was: The store is kept for a bad year and not for a bad week, a clerk in the hall says.
findings.now: The hall keeps the store for a bad year and not for a bad week, a clerk there says.
findings.why: The old line is passive and names no keeper — two readings fit it (the hall keeps the store; the trades keep it), so by 42b it makes no claim on that point. The new line commits to the hall. This is the pool's ONLY 42b sharpening and the implementer died before listing it, so it has been handed over to nobody; it is not covered by the old refutation and must be refuted. Flag for the refuter: V2 FACE 7 in the same variant has the guilds saying "the keeping of the store falls on the trades", so the chosen reading collides with a neighbouring face on the same word.
findings.readingChosen: The hall is the keeper. The pool's state supports it: V1 FACE 1 puts the key at the hall, V3 FACE 1 has the clerk saying that for the purpose of the door the hall is the town, and V3 FACE 6 has what comes in for the store passed on the hall's word. The competing reading (the trades keep it) is voiced only by the guilds, who are the interested party and whose own line separates keeping from deciding.
findings.proposedFix: The hall holds the store for a bad year and not for a bad week, a clerk there says.

findings.was: The stallholders say a store that is not drawn on in a dear year is a store kept for somebody other than the town.
findings.now: The stallholders say a store not drawn on in a dear year is kept for somebody other than the people at their boards.
findings.why: The beneficiary class narrows from the town to the market's own customers. The intent is right — 42d wants the stallholders' own party-word in the sentence — but the new line now permits a reading the old one forbade, that the store IS kept for the town at large and merely not for market folk. The stake can be had without shrinking the class.
findings.proposedFix: The stallholders say a store not drawn on in a dear year is kept for somebody other than the town they sell to.

findings.was: Who says when the granary door opens is answered one way at the hall and another at the market. The grain is in store and the door to it is kept.
findings.now: Who says when the store door opens is answered one way at the hall and another at the market. The grain is in store and the door to it is kept.
findings.why: The line was touched for 42c and left failing 42b. "is answered one way at the hall and another at the market" names neither answer — it is the brief's own worked example, "The town argues about this names no disagreement", in engine voice. A reader can act on nothing here. The two answers are already sitting in the pool and can simply be stated.
findings.proposedFix: At the hall the store door is said to open on the hall's word, at the market on the word of whoever fills it. The grain is in store and the door to it is kept.

findings.was: 27 of 27 faces in the shape "a role says a fact" before the cut
findings.now: 27 of 27 faces in the shape "a role says a fact" after the cut
findings.why: The brief's VARY THE SHAPE instruction was not executed on a single face. None of the lawful alternatives appears anywhere in the pool: nobody FINDS anything, nobody DOES anything, no face carries the bare fact. Worse, two cuts moved lines INTO the dominant frame — V1 FACE 4 went from the sayerless "the granary door is called the best kept thing" to "At the tavern they call", and V3 FACE 8 went from a mid-sentence attribution ("the guilds say" in the middle) to a front-loaded "The guilds say", spending one of the pool's few varied shapes. The owner's own six lines use four different shapes; this pool uses one.
findings.proposedFix: Convert two or three faces to shapes that keep the source as the actor rather than as a sayer, e.g. V1 FACE 6 to "A travelling trader gets the way to the grain store pointed out to him before the way to the inn." and V2 FACE 6 to "A carter asking the way to the house for the sick is walked there rather than pointed."

findings.was: the withholding tail on four faces
findings.now: "and leaves it there" · "and does not say where" · "and gives no reason for it" · "and does not say whether it would if asked"
findings.why: The same closing device — the speaker declines to say more — ends four faces, three of them consecutive-ish within variant 3 (FACES 4, 5 and 9 of nine). At that density it reads as a tic of the writer rather than as the concealment the law sanctions, and in V2 FACE 9 ("and leaves it there") it is not even a fact about the speaker, it is the writer telling the reader that the garrison said no more.
findings.proposedFix: Keep the device on V3 FACE 9, where the garrison's refusal is the face's whole point, and cut it from V2 FACE 9 and one of V3 FACE 4 or FACE 5.

findings.was: One of the garrison says the store is what a siege is about, and that the door to it is not the garrison's to hold.
findings.now: One of the garrison says the grain is what a siege is about, and the door to it is not his to hold.
findings.why: The old line makes an institutional claim — the garrison as a body does not hold the grain door, which is what V3 FACE 9 confirms ("nobody has asked it to guard the grain"). The new "not his to hold" narrows it to this one soldier's duty, which is a smaller and different fact. The pronoun is the right 42d instinct, but here the party-word was already doing that work and carried more.
findings.proposedFix: One of the garrison says the grain is what a siege is about, and the door to it is not the garrison's to hold.

untouchedFacesFailingTheStandard.text: A carter says that anyone asked the way to the house for the sick walks the asker there rather than pointing.
untouchedFacesFailingTheStandard.whichRule: 42d — the carter is nowhere in his own sentence. A reader can state the fact but cannot name what the carter stands to gain or lose; he is a bystander reporting on "anyone" and "the asker". Also the flattest available shape on a face whose source is the one source that can legitimately FIND something.
untouchedFacesFailingTheStandard.proposedFix: A carter says that when he asks the way to the house for the sick he is walked there rather than pointed.

untouchedFacesFailingTheStandard.text: The sick are taken in first and the wage settled after, the garrison says, and leaves it there.
untouchedFacesFailingTheStandard.whichRule: 42b and 42. "the wage" reads two ways — the fee owed for treating the man, or the soldier's pay — and the line commits to neither, so it makes no claim a reader can act on. And "and leaves it there" is the writer commenting on the speaker's silence rather than a fact the speaker gave.
untouchedFacesFailingTheStandard.proposedFix: The garrison says the sick are taken in first and what is owed for them is settled after.

untouchedFacesFailingTheStandard.text: A local priest holds that whoever takes the sick in answers somewhere other than the hall, and does not say where.
untouchedFacesFailingTheStandard.whichRule: 42d — nothing in the line says what the priest stands to gain or lose by the sick house answering elsewhere; his ground, his house and his own dealings with it are all absent. The claim itself is lawfully negative and can stand as it is.
untouchedFacesFailingTheStandard.proposedFix: A local priest holds that whoever takes the sick in answers somewhere other than the hall, and will not say so where the hall can hear it.

untouchedFacesFailingTheStandard.text: Whoever holds the way through says what comes in for the store is passed on the hall's word and asked nothing after.
untouchedFacesFailingTheStandard.whichRule: 42c in spirit — "Whoever holds the way through" is a riddle the reader has to solve before the fact arrives. The owner's own worked line uses the plain word: "the gatekeeper locks the gate at night". The periphrasis costs the reader the first half of the sentence and buys nothing.
untouchedFacesFailingTheStandard.proposedFix: The gatekeeper says what comes in for the store is passed on the hall's word and asked nothing after.

leastSure: "At the market they say the store door opens on the word of whoever fills it, and that the hall hears of it after the market does." — I read the market's precedence as a new fact, but a charitable reading is that "afterwards" already implied everyone else knew first, in which case this is wording, not a move.

"The hall keeps the store for a bad year and not for a bad week, a clerk there says." — I classed it a 42b sharpening rather than a claim move because the old passive genuinely left the keeper open, but the subject of the sentence changed from the store to the hall, and a stricter reading would call that a moved claim outright.

"One of the garrison says the grain is what a siege is about, and the door to it is not his to hold." — most readers will hear "his" as him-qua-garrison and lose nothing, so this may be a pronoun doing exactly what 42d asks rather than a narrowing worth reverting.

result.pool: Disasters & Famine: granary AND parish care only
result.summary: The cut is real but shallow, and it broke the freeze in two places. Mechanically the pool is clean: no em dash, no semicolon, no exclamation, no digit in prose, no contraction (every apostrophe hit is a possessive: town's, nobody's, stranger's), no first person, no will/shall, no bare "the priest"/"the mayor"/"the elder". The one archaism the brief names by hand, "a guild factor", was cured to "a guild member" in both places it occurred (V2 F5, V3 F5) — that is the single most valuable thing this cut did. Six faces had the "and that ..." tic deleted, which is the ruling-42 trailing-clause fix and is correct every time it was applied. Two faces were split into two sentences (V2 SPINE, V2 F4) and both survive the 42a delete-the-second-sentence test. Owner-standard pass rate moves 13 of 25 to 20 of 25. BUT: (1) V2 F7 [stranger] converts a habitual claim into a one-off past event, which the freeze names explicitly as a moved claim — BLOCKING; (2) V3 F1 [register] replaces "is given a person" with "is sent him instead", which is both garbled and swaps an unnamed person for the priest himself — BLOCKING; (3) three further faces narrow their subject to the speaker's own party (a drinker, the drinkers there, the garrison) — this looks like a 42d stake insertion but it shrinks the claim's scope and needs the chair's call; (4) the brief's loudest instruction, VARY THE SHAPE, was not obeyed at all: 23 of 25 lines are still "a role says a fact", and the implementer varied the attribution VERB instead of the shape (says became reckon, hold that, has it that, reports that, reckons), which in three cases made the line less plain than it was at HEAD. Only two untouched faces fail the standard, so the cut was not stopped short by the death — it was thin from the start.

findings.was: A traveller says that asking after the sick here gets a person and asking after the grain gets a building.
findings.now: A traveller says he asked after the sick here and was given a person, and asked after the grain and was given a building.
findings.why: The old line is habitual and general ("asking ... gets"): anyone who asks gets this result, every time. The new line is a single past event that happened to one traveller. The freeze names this exact case — "whether a thing is habitual or one-off" — as a moved claim, and a one-off no longer supports the standing refutation. The implementer was plainly reaching for the owner's FOUND shape ("A traveller found the steps to the wall blocked with stored grain"), which is the right instinct but was bought with the fact.
findings.proposedFix: A traveller found that asking after the sick here gets a person and asking after the grain gets a building.

findings.was: A local priest says a stranger asks for a house and is given a person, and that nobody born here asks for the house.
findings.now: A local priest says a stranger asks for a house and is sent him instead, and nobody born here asks for a house at all.
findings.why: Two faults in one line. "is given a person" becomes "is sent him instead", which moves the claim from an unnamed person to the speaking priest himself — a change of who is doing something. It is also ungrammatical enough to be unreadable: "is sent him" has no clear antecedent and can be parsed as "is sent to him", so the line has two readings and by 42b makes no claim. Separately "the house" widens to "a house at all", which drops the back-reference to the house the stranger asked for.
findings.proposedFix: A local priest says a stranger asks for a house and is given a person instead, and nobody born here asks for the house.

findings.was: HEAD: 22 of 25 lines in the frame "a role says a fact"
findings.now: AFTER: 23 of 25 lines in the frame "a role says a fact"
findings.why: The brief's boldest instruction is AND VARY THE SHAPE, with five lawful alternatives named. The cut used none of them. The only bare-fact line in the pool (V1 SPINE) was already there at HEAD; no line became someone FOUND something, someone DOES something, or nobody HAS DONE something. What the implementer actually varied was the attribution verb: "say" became "reckon" (V1 F2), "hold that" (V1 F5), "has it that" (V1 F4), "reports that" (V1 F7) and "reckons" (V3 F5). Five faces changed nothing but that verb, which spends the cut without moving toward the standard and installs a new tic in place of the old one. The monotony is the defect the brief says is invisible pool by pool and obvious six at a time — this pool contributes almost nothing but the monotonous frame.
findings.proposedFix: Restore the plain "says" on the five verb-only edits and buy the variation from shape instead. Two candidates inside the freeze: V1 F7 as a DOES line — "One of those on the gate lets a cart carrying for the store through his gate ahead of a cart carrying for a stall, he says." — and V3 F4's fact as a NOBODY-HAS-DONE line, which it already half is.

findings.was: The garrison says the store is the one thing here worth standing in front of, and that standing in front of it is nobody's order.
findings.now: The garrison says the store is the one thing here worth standing in front of, and nobody has ordered it to.
findings.why: The edit removed the "and that" tic correctly but introduced a pronoun collision. In "nobody has ordered it to", the nearest antecedent for "it" is "the store", not the garrison, and the infinitive after "to" is elided. Two readings fit the sentence, so by 42b it makes no claim. This vagueness is new — it was not in the HEAD line.
findings.proposedFix: The garrison says the store is the one thing here worth standing in front of, and nobody has ordered the garrison to stand there.

findings.was: ... and that standing in front of it is nobody's order.
findings.now: ... and nobody has ordered it to.
findings.readingChosen: Reading taken: no order has been given TO THE GARRISON. The rejected reading is the wider one the HEAD line carried — that no order to guard the store exists for anyone at all. The pool's state supports the narrower reading: the garrison is the only armed body on any card in this pool, so an order to stand in front of the store would fall to it, and the face is sourced [garrison]. It still needs refuting because the narrower claim asserts something about the garrison's own orders that the wider claim did not.
findings.why: Recorded here as a sharpening rather than a breach because the old line's "nobody's order" was scope-vague and the new line commits to one reading. It is therefore NOT covered by the standing refutation and must go to the refuter with the rest of the 42b list.

findings.was: At the tavern they say the one who comes to sit up and the one who comes to dig are the same trade.
findings.now: At the tavern they say the man who sits up with a drinker and the man who digs for him are the same trade.
findings.why: The old claim is general: whoever sits up with the sick and whoever digs the grave are one trade, for anybody. The new claim is about a drinker — the tavern's own patron. The trade identity survives but the class of people tended shrinks from the whole parish to the tavern's custom, which is a change of how much. The motive is visibly 42d (putting the tavern's own party-word in the sentence), but 42d says the stake must be drawn from what the source already is, not bought by narrowing the fact.
findings.proposedFix: At the tavern they say the man who comes to sit up with the sick and the man who digs for them are the same trade.

findings.was: At the tavern they say strangers walk up to look at the store, and that nobody here does.
findings.now: At the tavern they say strangers walk up to look at the store, and no drinker there has ever bothered.
findings.why: "nobody here" means nobody in the town; "no drinker there" means nobody in that tavern. The claim shrinks from a statement about the whole settlement to a statement about one room of it. Same pattern as V2 F3: a 42d stake bought with the claim's scope. The "and that" removal and the plainer "has ever bothered" are both good and should be kept.
findings.proposedFix: At the tavern they say strangers walk up to look at the store, and nobody in the town has ever bothered.

findings.was: A local priest says the store has a door and a lock. The tending has neither.
findings.now: A local priest has it that the store has a door and a lock. The tending has neither.
findings.why: This is the one edit that made a line worse. "has it that" is a fusty attribution formula, not a plain modern word, and 42c withdrew that licence; every one of the owner's six worked lines uses "says". It also downgrades the priest from a man stating a fact about his own work to a source of hearsay, which weakens the attribution the freeze protects. The HEAD line was already at the owner's standard and needed nothing.
findings.proposedFix: A local priest says the store has a door and a lock. The tending he does has neither.

findings.was: F1: A local priest says the tending falls to the parish and is paid for by nobody. / F2 WAS: A clerk in the hall says the tending is what a parish is for, and that the purse has no line in it for a parish.
findings.now: F1 unchanged. / F2 NOW: A clerk in the hall says the tending is what a parish is for, and the purse has no line in it for a parish.
findings.why: The pair is tagged "disagree" but the two faces agree on every fact in evidence: the parish does the tending, and nobody pays for it. What separates them is attitude — the priest treats it as a burden, the clerk as the proper order of things. By 42b that is exactly "the town argues about this": it names no disagreement a reader can act on. This pre-dates the cut, and the cut (a "that" deletion) did not address it. Note that the identical hall/parish material is tagged "reinforce" for pair 1 in VARIANT 1, which is what these two actually do.
findings.proposedFix: Either re-tag pair 1 in VARIANT 2 as reinforce, which is what the two lines honestly are, or give the clerk a fact the priest denies. The nearest one inside the pool's state: "A clerk in the hall says the parish asked for the tending and has never asked the purse for it." — flagged as a NEW claim needing refutation, not a freeze-safe edit.

findings.was: A clerk in the hall says the store is the town's to keep and not the town's to open.
findings.now: A clerk in the hall says the store the hall keeps is the town's, and not the town's to open.
findings.why: Recorded for the chair rather than pressed as a breach. The old line said the store is the town's to keep; the new one names the hall as the keeper and the town as the owner. Those are the same fact in a settlement where the hall is the town's own body, and the insertion is a textbook 42d move (the clerk's own house in his own sentence). But the freeze lists "a change of who is doing something" as a move, and this is the only line in the pool where the doer of an action changed. If the chair reads the freeze strictly, revert; if it reads 42d as licensing the speaker's own party-word, keep.
findings.proposedFix: A clerk in the hall says the store is the town's to keep and not the town's to open.

findings.was: Everyone here has seen the store door and nobody here has seen it stand open, and everyone here knows that a sickness in a house is answered by whoever the parish sends.
findings.now: Everyone here has seen the store door and nobody here has seen it stand open. A sickness in a house is answered by whoever the parish sends.
findings.why: The split is right and the second sentence survives the 42a test on its own. But "everyone here knows that" was dropped, so a claim the street held is now a bare narrator assertion. Defensible under ruling 40 — this is an engine fact, and VARIANT 1's spine states the same fact bare — and this is a spine rather than a sourced face, so no card attribution was lost. Flagged only so the chair sees that the cut did touch an attribution, given the previous cure's history.
findings.proposedFix: Everyone here has seen the store door and nobody here has seen it stand open. Everyone here knows a sickness in a house is answered by whoever the parish sends.

findings.was: One of those on the gate says a cart carrying for the store goes through ahead of a cart carrying for a stall.
findings.now: One of those on the gate reports that a cart carrying for the store goes through ahead of a cart carrying for a stall.
findings.why: A plainness regression with no gain. "reports that" is longer, more bureaucratic and less plain than "says", and it re-inserts the subordinating "that" the cut spent six other edits removing. The HEAD line already passed. If the face was going to be touched at all, the available win was 42d — the gateman's own gate is nowhere in his sentence.
findings.proposedFix: One of those on the gate says a cart carrying for the store goes through his gate ahead of a cart carrying for a stall.

findings.was: At the tavern they say one hand holds the key to the store, and that nobody at the table knows the hand.
findings.now: At the tavern they say one hand holds the key to the store, and nobody at the table knows the hand.
findings.why: The "and that" removal is correct. What was left behind is the crafted-before-clear figure the ruling is named for: a hand holds the key and nobody knows the hand. The owner's worked lines are all concrete people and things — a clerk, a gatekeeper, steps, grain. "the hand" for "the man" is the writer performing. The line was touched, so the plain version was there to be taken.
findings.proposedFix: At the tavern they say one man holds the key to the store, and nobody at the table knows which man.

findings.was: A guild factor says what a stranger takes for provision is a store the trades filled and cannot open.
findings.now: A guild member reckons what a stranger takes for provision is a store the trades filled and cannot open.
findings.why: The 42c cure (factor to member) is correct and is the point of the edit. Left standing is the writerly inversion "what a stranger takes for provision is ...", which makes the reader assemble the subject before the fact arrives. The claim is recoverable but the sentence is built the crafted way round, and "reckons" adds nothing.
findings.proposedFix: A guild member says the store a stranger takes for provision is one the trades filled and cannot open.

untouchedFacesFailingTheStandard.text: Grain is hard to keep here, those who sell at the market say, for anybody without a door of their own in the town.
untouchedFacesFailingTheStandard.whichRule: 42 (the qualifier is in a trailing clause, not inside the sentence) and 42b ("hard to keep" measures nothing — it fits both "costs more" and "cannot be done at all"). The qualifier "for anybody without a door of their own in the town" trails after both the fact and the attribution, which is the shape ruling 42 names outright.
untouchedFacesFailingTheStandard.proposedFix: Those who sell at the market say a man without a door of his own in the town has nowhere to keep grain. NOTE: this is a 42b sharpening, not a freeze-safe edit — it commits to the reading that such a man cannot keep grain at all rather than that it merely costs him, and must go to the refuter.

untouchedFacesFailingTheStandard.text: Those who hear disputes say a stranger's questions about the store are ordinary and the ones about the sick are new to them.
untouchedFacesFailingTheStandard.whichRule: 42d (no stake). From the line alone a reader cannot say what the dispute-hearers gain or lose, and nothing in the sentence is theirs — not their court, not their disputes, not even the asking. It is also the one face in the pool whose source is unexplained: why strangers' questions reach the people who hear disputes is not on the page.
untouchedFacesFailingTheStandard.proposedFix: Those who hear the town's disputes say a stranger's questions to them about the store are ordinary, and the ones about the sick are new to them.

leastSure: "A clerk in the hall says the store the hall keeps is the town's, and not the town's to open." — I cannot tell whether naming the hall as keeper is the 42d stake the brief asks for or the change-of-doer the freeze forbids; it turns on how the chair reads the hall as an organ of the town.

"The garrison says the store is the one thing here worth standing in front of, and nobody has ordered it to." — a reader who takes "it" as the garrison gets a clean line, and I may be over-reading the collision with "the store"; the narrowing behind it is the part I am sure about.

"At the tavern they say the man who sits up with a drinker and the man who digs for him are the same trade." — the tavern's own drinker is exactly the party-word 42d wants in the sentence, and I am calling it a scope move; if the card's fact is about the parish's tender rather than about who is tended, the narrowing may be harmless.

result.summary: The cut is mostly sound and it moved the pool a long way: by my own reading of the owner's standard, 13 of the 34 lines (31 faces plus 3 spines) passed before and 26 pass now. The named 42c vocabulary sweep is COMPLETE and clean — pedlar, sexton (both sites), factor and night patrolman are gone, with no new archaism and no mechanical bar breached anywhere in the NOW text (verified by grep: no em dash, exclamation, digit, semicolon, contraction, first person, will/shall). Both disagreement pairs still genuinely disagree after the cut (pair 1: the common purse alone and first, against the trades carrying as much; pair 2: the ground paid before everything, against the ground waiting its turn in the queue). ONE BLOCKING DEFECT: variant 3 face 5 [tavern] swapped the speaker — the drinkers who reported a fact about a third group were replaced by that group speaking for itself, which is both a moved claim and a dropped attribution, and it must be reverted before this lands. The cut's real shortfall is not error but omission. It did almost no 42b work: exactly one line got sharpened (variant 3 face 4, where a passive acquired an agent), and the vague lines that 42b exists to catch were left standing ("the bar gets looked to first and counted last", "the place meets what it is asked for, and meets it short", "never been called for worse than they know"). It also did no shape work at all: all 31 faces are still a role asserting a fact, none uses the FOUND or DOES shape the owner's own worked lines show, and eight of the 22 edits went the wrong way by converting "X's account is that" into a plain "X says", which spends the surface variety HEAD had without buying any structural variety back. Both stranger faces describe a found thing and could take the FOUND shape at zero claim cost. Finally the cut fixed the words on the 42c list and did not apply the rule behind them: "the ordinary" survives in three faces, two of which the implementer had open at the time, and it is the least plain word left in the pool. The death looks to have come after the mechanical substitutions and before the judgment passes.

findings.was: Drinkers at the tavern say the people who would be wanted first if trouble came are the people who already have work enough.
findings.now: At the tavern the men who would be wanted first if trouble came say they already have work enough.
findings.why: The speaker changed. WAS, third parties (drinkers) report a fact about a different group; NOW that group reports on itself, so a general observation about the town's labour has become a self-report by the men who would be called. A change of who is doing the saying is a moved claim, and the drinkers as the attributed speaker were deleted outright, which the freeze forbids separately. The old refutation was run against a drinkers' observation and no longer covers this line. The instinct was right, since the drinkers have a thin stake under 42d, but 42d must be satisfied without taking the speaker off the card.
findings.proposedFix: Drinkers at the tavern say the men who would be wanted first if trouble came already have work enough.

findings.was: A guild factor holds that the ordinary is drawn as much from the trades as from the purse.
findings.now: A guild member holds that the ordinary is drawn as much from the trades as from the purse.
findings.why: The listed word was fixed and the unlisted one in the same sentence was not. "The ordinary", meaning the settlement's routine expenditure, is a historical accounting term no modern reader will parse, and 42c is a rule about plain modern words, not a closed list of five. It stands in three faces: this one, variant 1 face 4 (untouched) and variant 3 face 4 (touched). Variant 3 face 4 is the worst of them, since "opened the store for the ordinary" reads as an unfinished phrase. Claim is unaffected by the swap. If "the ordinary" is a card term rather than prose, the chair should say so and these three stand.
findings.proposedFix: A guild member holds that the everyday costs are drawn as much from the trades as from the purse.

findings.faceOrSpine: POOL — all 31 faces, all three variants
findings.was: HEAD carried some surface variety: "By the account of those who hold the way through", "Asked at the guilds, they say", "The hall's own answer is that", "By the soldiers' own account".
findings.now: All four are now "Those who hold the way through say", "The guilds say", "A clerk in the hall holds", "The soldiers report".
findings.why: The brief's VARY THE SHAPE instruction was not exercised. All 31 faces are a role asserting a fact; no face uses the FOUND shape of the owner's "A traveller found the steps to the wall blocked with stored grain", and none uses the bare DOES shape of "Local families repair the walls and are paid nothing". Eight of the 22 edits made this worse by flattening the stiffer attribution frames into a plain "X says", spending the variety HEAD had without buying structural variety back. The two stranger faces are the cheapest fix: both already describe a found thing, and the FOUND shape keeps the speaker attributed, so it costs no claim and breaks no freeze.
findings.proposedFix: Variant 1 face 1: A travelling trader found the trestle he was lent at the market mended where it broke, and it carried his whole load. · Variant 3 face 1: A drover found a bed for himself and shelter for his beasts without anyone going out of their way. Nothing he was given was more than he needed.

findings.was: Those who set out a stall say the share is paid before the selling is done, and that the complaint comes to the stall because the stall is what stands still.
findings.now: Those who set out a stall say the share is paid before the selling is done. The complaint comes to the stall, the stall being what stands still.
findings.why: The explainer survived the cut and changed costume. "Because the stall is what stands still" became the absolute "the stall being what stands still", which is still a trailing clause telling the reader what to make of the sentence before it, and the participial absolute is a more mannered construction than the one it replaced. 42 requires the qualifier inside the sentence or gone. Cutting it removes no fact: the facts are that the share is paid in advance and that the complaint lands on the stall.
findings.proposedFix: Those who set out a stall say the share is paid before the selling is done. The complaint comes to the stall.

findings.was: The sexton's account is that the ground is opened for whoever needs it. The boards laid over a new plot are the boards laid over the last one.
findings.now: Whoever keeps the ground has it that it is opened for whoever needs it. The boards laid over a new plot are the boards laid over the last one.
findings.why: The 42c substitution is right and the sentence it produced is not clear. "Whoever ... whoever" in eleven words, plus "has it that it is opened" where the pronoun sits two nouns from its referent, is craft before clarity. The same implementer wrote the clean version of this construction at variant 2 face 1 ("Whoever keeps the ground says it is paid for before anything else here is"), so this is an inconsistency rather than a misreading of the rule. "Has it that" also appears at variant 1 face 7; once in a pool is voice, twice is a tic. Claim is untouched by the fix.
findings.proposedFix: Whoever keeps the ground says it is opened for anyone who needs it. The boards laid over a new plot are the boards laid over the last one.

findings.was: At the hall the word is that the store has been opened for the ordinary and for nothing else.
findings.now: A clerk in the hall says the hall has opened the store for the ordinary and for nothing else.
findings.why: The passive named no agent; the new line supplies one, so the claim is now definite where it was open and the old refutation does not cover it. This is the pool's ONLY 42b sharpening and it must be collected for refuting. Two further problems ride on the same line: "a clerk in the hall says the hall" repeats the noun inside nine words, and the opener is now word for word identical to variant 1 face 4's untouched "A clerk in the hall says", a cross-variant collision the cut created (HEAD had three different hall openers across the three variants). "The ordinary" also survives here and reads worst of its three sites.
findings.readingChosen: The hall is the agent that opened the store. The pool's state supports it: the source card is [hall], and variant 1 face 4 has the hall's own clerk saying the everyday costs are met out of the common purse, so the store's opening for those costs sits with the hall rather than with any other party in the pool.
findings.proposedFix: Keep the sharpening and fix the rest: A clerk in the hall says the hall has opened its store for the town's everyday needs and for nothing else. Or drop the sharpening and the refutation debt with it: A clerk in the hall holds that the store has been opened for the town's everyday needs and for nothing else.

findings.was: By the account of those who hold the way through, the bar gets looked to first and counted last.
findings.now: Those who hold the way through say the bar gets looked to first and counted last.
findings.why: The frame was plainened and the vague half was left. "Counted last" carries two readings a reader cannot choose between: last in the accounts, meaning paid for after everything else, or last in a tally of what the town has. 42b says a line with two readings makes no claim. The pool's own state supports the money reading, since every neighbouring face is about who pays and in what order.
findings.readingChosen: Last in the purse, that is, paid for after everything else. The pool is an economic-survival pool and its other gate, hall, market and register faces all turn on order of payment, so the accounting reading is the one the state supports.
findings.proposedFix: Those who hold the way through say the bar gets looked to first and paid for last.

findings.was: Those who turn out for the muster say they have never been called for worse than they know, and that they would come for worse.
findings.now: Those who turn out for the muster say they have never been called for worse than they know, and they would come for worse.
findings.why: The edit dropped one "that" and left the hard part. "Called for worse than they know" needs a second pass to parse, and "worse" doing duty as a bare noun twice in one sentence is craft before clarity. The claim is definite once decoded, so this is a plainness finding rather than a two-readings one, but it is one of the lines that shows the cut stopped at the mechanical level.
findings.proposedFix: Those who turn out for the muster say they have never been called out for anything worse than what they already know, and they would come for worse.

findings.was: The soldiers' account is that the town gives what it has and says nothing about the rest.
findings.now: The soldiers reckon the town gives what it has and says nothing about the rest.
findings.why: An account is testimony and a reckoning is an estimate, so the edit shades the soldiers from reporting what they receive to guessing at it. The fact about the town does not move, which is why this is a note and not a block, but under a regime where faces are refuted against cards the evidential force of the reporting verb is part of what gets refuted. Plain "say" keeps the force and is plainer than either. "Reckon" is also used at variant 3 face 6, where it is the right word because HEAD said "reckoning".
findings.proposedFix: The soldiers say the town gives what it has and says nothing about the rest.

untouchedFacesFailingTheStandard.text: A clerk in the hall says the ordinary is provided for out of the common purse, and provided for first.
untouchedFacesFailingTheStandard.whichRule: 42c — "the ordinary" is a historical accounting term, not a plain modern word. The line is otherwise exactly the owner's model shape and needs only the noun swapped. Must move together with variant 1 face 5 and variant 3 face 4 so pair 1 keeps matching vocabulary on both sides of the disagreement.
untouchedFacesFailingTheStandard.proposedFix: A clerk in the hall says the everyday costs are met out of the common purse, and met first.

untouchedFacesFailingTheStandard.text: The quarrels brought before those who hear them are about who pays, they say, and never about whether there is anything to pay with.
untouchedFacesFailingTheStandard.whichRule: 42 — clear before crafted. The sentence buries its speaker in the middle as a bare "they say" whose antecedent is "those who hear them", itself sitting after "the quarrels", so the reader resolves two pronouns before reaching the fact. It is the most convoluted line the cut left alone, and it is the one untouched face I would call a clear miss rather than a judgment call.
untouchedFacesFailingTheStandard.proposedFix: Those who hear disputes say the quarrels brought to them are about who pays, and never about whether there is anything to pay with.

untouchedFacesFailingTheStandard.text: The place meets what it is asked for, and meets it short.
untouchedFacesFailingTheStandard.whichRule: 42 and 42b — "meets it short" is a compression no modern speaker would produce, and the sentence names no thing, sum or act, which is what the owner's worked lines never fail to do. Variants 2 and 3 spines both pass. Flagged with the caveat that spines are the pool's thesis line and the chair may hold them exempt from the face standard.
untouchedFacesFailingTheStandard.proposedFix: The place meets what it is asked for, and meets it with nothing to spare.

untouchedFacesFailingTheStandard.text: Whoever holds the way through says the bar is worked by whoever the turn falls to. The turn comes round to everybody.
untouchedFacesFailingTheStandard.whichRule: 42 and possibly 42c — "whoever ... whoever" in one clause, and "whoever holds the way through" is a circumlocution where the owner's own worked line uses the plain "the gatekeeper". Low confidence: "whoever keeps the ground" is the prescribed replacement for sexton, so the pool may be applying that precedent deliberately to the gate, and the mechanical bar on definite singular roles names only priest, mayor and elder. The chair should rule rather than the implementer guess.
untouchedFacesFailingTheStandard.proposedFix: A gatekeeper says the bar is worked by whoever the turn falls to. The turn comes round to everybody.

leastSure: "The complaint comes to the stall, the stall being what stands still." — I read the absolute clause as the same explainer 42 bans, wearing a participle instead of a "because"; a chair could as easily read it as a qualifier now folded into the sentence, which is what 42 asks for.

"A clerk in the hall says the hall has opened the store for the ordinary and for nothing else." — whether supplying an agent to a passive counts as a 42b sharpening that owes a refutation, or is a neutral voice change inside the freeze, is the call I am least confident of in the whole pool.

"The soldiers reckon the town gives what it has and says nothing about the rest." — report becoming estimate may be beneath the grain the freeze is meant to police, in which case this line should simply stand.

result.pool: Disasters & Famine: NO reserves, hospital present
result.summary: Ten faces were cut, three spines were never touched, and the header's counts are accurate (10 changed + 5 unchanged = 15 faces, 3 spines, 18 lines). The cut is real work: both `pedlar` archaisms are gone, four trailing "and that ..." clauses became separate sentences in the owner's own two-sentence shape, and one unattributed "the talk is" got a named speaker. By my judgment the pool goes from 6 of 18 lines passing the owner's standard to 12 of 18. But the claim freeze did NOT hold twice, and both breaks have the same signature: the implementer reached for the speaker's own party-word (42d's move, which is not even in the brief it was given) and paid for it with the claim. In VARIANT 2 FACE 4 the town's water ("the water is fetched from whichever source runs clean") became the tavern's own water ("they fetch their water"), shrinking a settlement fact to one building; in VARIANT 1 FACE 4 what "everybody here knows" became what "everybody at the table" knows, shrinking town-wide common knowledge to the drinkers who are already saying it. Two more faces were touched without curing the defect that made them worth touching: VARIANT 2 FACE 2 lost "against the parish" but kept the explaining clause (and is now vaguer for it), and VARIANT 3 FACE 1 lost "therefore" but kept the clause the "therefore" was flagging. The cut also ran the wrong way on shape: it converted three non-"say" openers ("Among the elders the account is", "The tavern's own account is", "On market day the talk is") into "say"/"hold that", so 13 of 15 faces are now a role-asserts-a-fact frame against the brief's explicit instruction to vary. Finally the cut is INCOMPLETE, not merely imperfect: two of three spines and two untouched faces still fail the standard outright, and the spines were never opened at all (spines changed 0 of 3), which is consistent with a death partway through rather than a finished pass. Two 42b-adjacent sharpenings need collecting for re-refutation; neither is covered by the old refutation. Both disagreement pairs still genuinely disagree after the cut.

findings.was: The tavern's own account is that the water is fetched from whichever source runs clean, and that what is not clean can be made so for a price.
findings.now: At the tavern they say they fetch their water from whichever source runs clean. What is not clean can be made so for a price.
findings.why: The old line's passive "the water is fetched" is a fact about the settlement's water; "they fetch their water" makes it a fact about the tavern's own bucket. That is a change of who is doing something and of scope, which the freeze names as a moved claim. It also drags the second sentence with it: "what is not clean" now reads as the tavern's supply, not the town's. If this was an attempt at the speaker's stake, it bought the stake with the whole claim.
findings.proposedFix: At the tavern they say the water here is fetched from whichever source runs clean. They say what is not clean can be made so for a price.

findings.was: At the tavern they say a house sends for the parish when it cannot settle with the healers, and that everybody here knows which house is which.
findings.now: At the tavern they say a house sends for the parish when it cannot settle with the healers. Everybody at the table knows which house is which.
findings.why: Splitting the trailing clause into its own sentence is correct and matches the owner's worked lines, but "everybody here" (the town, spoken by townspeople) became "everybody at the table" (the drinkers). That narrows how many people hold the knowledge, and it narrows it to the degenerate reading: of course the table knows what the table is saying. The face's fact was that a household's inability to pay the healers is public knowledge in the town.
findings.proposedFix: At the tavern they say a house sends for the parish when it cannot settle with the healers. They say everybody here knows which house is which.

findings.was: The older households hold that the tending falls to the neighbours first and the parish last, and that saying so is no complaint against the parish.
findings.now: The older households hold that the tending falls to the neighbours first and the parish last, and that saying so is no complaint.
findings.why: The clause the cut should have removed is still there. "and that saying so is no complaint" carries no fact: it is the writer telling the reader how to take the first clause, which 42 says must be gone. Deleting the words "against the parish" made it worse rather than better, because the disclaimer now has no object and states even less. The pair still disagrees either way, so cutting the clause costs nothing.
findings.proposedFix: The older households hold that the tending falls to the neighbours first and the parish last.

findings.was: Among the elders the account is that the strips are laid out so that no house is favoured, and that a short year is therefore short for every house.
findings.now: The elders say the strips are laid out so that no house is favoured, and a short year is short for every house.
findings.why: Removing "therefore" removed the signpost and left the thing it was pointing at. Apply 42a's test to the clause: if no house is favoured in the layout of the strips, then a short year being short for every house follows with no new fact added. It is the writer drawing the conclusion for the reader, which 42 forbids whether or not the word "therefore" is present. Cutting a clause that carried no independent fact does not move the claim.
findings.proposedFix: The elders say the strips are laid out so that no house is favoured.

findings.was: Among the elders the account is that ... / The tavern's own account is that ... / On market day the talk is that ...
findings.now: The elders say ... / At the tavern they say ... / On market day the stallholders say ...
findings.why: The brief's "AND VARY THE SHAPE" was run backwards. The cut converted three of the pool's few non-asserting openers into "say"/"hold that", so 13 of 15 faces are now a role-asserts-a-fact frame and only two use another lawful shape (VARIANT 1 FACE 2 and VARIANT 3 FACE 3 both found something; VARIANT 2 FACE 3 is a received answer). The owner's complaint was four in seven; this pool is now thirteen in fifteen. At least one of the three conversions should go to a different lawful shape without deleting the speaker.
findings.proposedFix: VARIANT 3 FACE 2: At the parish nobody weighs the tithe until the wheel has taken its share.

findings.faceOrSpine: POOL (worst: V1 FACE 1, V2 FACE 3, V3 FACE 1, V3 FACE 4)
findings.was: n/a - a gap in the brief, not a single line
findings.now: n/a
findings.why: The brief at kit/briefs/brief-block-clarity-recut.md states rulings 42, 42a, 42b, 42c and the shape rule, and contains NO 42d and none of 42's stake language. The implementer therefore cut the whole block without the speaker's-stake test, which explains both claim moves above: where it did reach for a party-word ("they fetch THEIR water", "everybody at the TABLE") it had no rule telling it the stake must be drawn from the card without disturbing the fact. Several lines state a fact from which no reader can name what the speaker gains or loses: "One of the elders says the answer to a hungry year here is the next house along", "a travelling trader was given the name of a household and no other answer", "The elders say the strips are laid out so that no house is favoured", "A carter at the tavern says the price for closing a wound is the same price in a bad year". The chair should repair the brief before any further pool is cut, or 42d will be missing from all 24.
findings.proposedFix: Add 42d and 42's stake clause to brief-block-clarity-recut.md verbatim before the next batch, and re-sweep the already-cut pools for stake only.

findings.was: A pedlar says the next house along has the same fields and the same year as the first.
findings.now: A travelling trader says he found the next house along with the same fields and the same year as the first.
findings.why: The 42c fix is required and correct. But "says he found" adds that the speaker was there himself, which the old line did not claim - he could have been repeating what he was told. The fact about the next house along is unchanged, so this is a small evidential sharpening rather than a moved claim, but it is not covered by the old refutation and must be collected.
findings.readingChosen: The reading that the trader speaks from having been there. The pool's state supports it: the source is the [stranger] card, whose whole nature is arriving from outside and having passed the next house along on the way in, and VARIANT 3 FACE 3 already has a traveller reporting what he finds coming in.

findings.was: On market day the talk is that nobody here buys against a year that has not come.
findings.now: On market day the stallholders say nobody here buys against a year that has not come.
findings.why: A good change - "the talk is" named no speaker, and the new line names one. But it does specify WHO holds the claim where the old line left it floating, so it is a sharpening and needs collecting, not freezing.
findings.readingChosen: The reading that the market's sellers are the speakers, not the buyers or the town at large. The [market] source tag supports it and VARIANT 2 FACE 5 already puts a stallholder in the speaking seat for this pool.

findings.was: Those who sell at the market say the same sacks that come off the wheel go out of the town.
findings.now: Those who sell at the market reckon the same sacks that come off the wheel go out of the town.
findings.why: The only change in this face is "say" to "reckon". It buys nothing the standard asks for and it hedges: "say" reports an assertion, "reckon" reports a guess, so the line commits slightly less than it did. If the intent was to break up the repeated "say", the shape should have changed rather than the certainty.
findings.proposedFix: Those who sell at the market say the same sacks that come off the wheel go out of the town. The households that sold them buy meal back later at the day's price.

findings.was: At the parish they say the tithe is weighed after the wheel has taken its share and not before.
findings.now: At the parish they hold that the tithe is weighed after the wheel has taken its share and not before.
findings.why: Churn with a small cost. This face already passed the standard; the only change swaps "say" for "hold that", which is the less plain of the two and duplicates the construction already used in VARIANT 1 FACE 3 and VARIANT 2 FACE 2. 42c asks for the plain modern word. Either revert it or spend the edit on shape instead.
findings.proposedFix: At the parish they say the tithe is weighed after the wheel has taken its share and not before.

untouchedFacesFailingTheStandard.text: The grain at {settlement} is grown, ground and eaten, and none of it stops anywhere in between. What the town keeps ready instead is a person.
untouchedFacesFailingTheStandard.whichRule: 42b - "a person" is a riddle, not a claim. A healer, a gravedigger, a priest and a midwife all fit it, so the sentence commits to none of them and the reader cannot act on it.
untouchedFacesFailingTheStandard.proposedFix: The grain at {settlement} is grown, ground and eaten, and none of it stops anywhere in between. What the town keeps ready instead is a healer. [42b SHARPENING - collect for refutation. The pool's own state supports "a healer": the pool is the hospital-present combination, VARIANT 1 FACE 4 has households settling with "the healers", and VARIANT 3 FACE 4 prices "closing a wound".]

untouchedFacesFailingTheStandard.text: Everyone here knows who is sent for when a body goes down. Why nothing was ever laid in against a bad harvest is a question the town does not answer.
untouchedFacesFailingTheStandard.whichRule: 42b - the second sentence states that no explanation exists rather than stating a fact, which is the "the town argues about this" failure: it names no answer and no disagreement, and there is nothing in it for a reader to act on.
untouchedFacesFailingTheStandard.proposedFix: Everyone here knows who is sent for when a body goes down. Nothing has ever been laid in here against a bad harvest.

untouchedFacesFailingTheStandard.text: A person of the parish holds that the ones who come to sit up and the ones who come to dig are the same hands, and does not say what that costs them.
untouchedFacesFailingTheStandard.whichRule: 42 - "and does not say what that costs them" adds no fact. It is the writer nudging the reader to notice a silence, which is the purest form of what 42 strikes. The sit-up/dig fact stands on its own without it.
untouchedFacesFailingTheStandard.proposedFix: A person of the parish says the ones who come to sit up with the sick and the ones who come to dig the graves are the same hands.

untouchedFacesFailingTheStandard.text: One of the elders says the answer to a hungry year here is the next house along.
untouchedFacesFailingTheStandard.whichRule: 42b and 42d - "the answer ... is the next house along" has at least two readings (they send grain, or they take the people in) and commits to neither, and nothing in the line lets a reader name what the elders gain or lose by saying it.
untouchedFacesFailingTheStandard.proposedFix: One of the elders says a house that runs short here gets its grain from the next house along. [42b SHARPENING - collect for refutation. The grain reading is the one the pool supports: its paired face answers on the same ground, "the next house along has the same fields and the same year", which only bites if what is wanted from that house is grain.]

leastSure: "Those who sell at the market reckon the same sacks that come off the wheel go out of the town." - I called the say/reckon swap a hedge rather than a moved claim, and a chair could reasonably rule that dropping from assertion to estimate does move the fact.

"A travelling trader says he found the next house along with the same fields and the same year as the first." - I filed "he found" as a small sharpening needing refutation, but it is arguable that it is plain 42d stake-work inside the freeze and needs nothing.

"Everybody at the table knows which house is which." - I ruled "here" meant the town and so called this a narrowing; if "here" was always the tavern, this is a lawful 42b sharpening and not a claim move at all.

result.summary: 27 faces and 3 spines; 9 faces changed, 0 spines. Mechanically the cut is clean: no em dash, exclamation, digit, semicolon, contraction, first person, will/shall, literal settlement token, or bare priest/mayor/singular elder anywhere in the pool (every apostrophe in the file is a possessive), and none of the struck archaisms (granary, infirmary, pedlar, factor, watchman, sexton, alehouse, bier, billhook, gaol, night patrolman) appear in either column. The face-count register is untouched: no face added, removed or re-sourced. Both pairs survive: V1 pair 1 (elders say the turn reaches everyone who can spare a back / the tavern says it reaches only the same backs) still genuinely disagrees, and is sharper now that the aggrieved party carries the tavern half; V3 pair 3 (register and elders on burials) is untouched and still reinforces. ONE BLOCKING defect: V2 FACE 1 re-scoped the claim from "what is put into a hand here" to "what is put into a stranger's hand here", confining in-kind giving to visitors, a reading the pool's own state contradicts (this pool is about households making up the difference for each other), and it is not covered by the old refutation. The shape of the cut is the more important finding. Six of the nine edits (V1 F7, V1 F8, V2 F3, V2 F5, V2 F8, V3 F8) are comma-to-period splits of trailing and-clauses that already carried a new fact, so they were already lawful under 42a and the split buys legibility, not a standard crossing. Only three edits (V1 F3, V1 F6 and the attempt at V2 F1) went after 42d, the rule this pool most fails. Net effect on the owner's own test: 19 of 30 lines before, 21 of 30 after, and seven of the nine lines that still fail were never touched at all, including the V2 spine, both market faces and all three elders faces. The cut was aimed at the wrong rule and stopped short. Pool-wide, all 27 faces after the cut are still some form of "a role says a fact"; the cut introduced not one FOUND, DOES, bare-engine or nobody-has-done shape, and V2 FACE 5 moved the pool's only fact-first line into the leading-attribution frame.

findings.was: What is put into a hand here is goods and not coin, a stranger says, and no apology comes with the sack.
findings.now: What is put into a stranger's hand here is goods and not coin, he says, and he got no apology with the sack.
findings.why: The old line was vague about whose hand, so a sharpening was owed, but the implementer committed to the reading the pool's state does not support: confining in-kind giving to visitors. The pool is about households covering each other (V1 spine, the ask made out loud in front of the neighbours, the loudest household asked last), not hospitality to strangers. The trailing clause additionally moves a habitual practice (no apology comes with the sack) to a single past event (he got no apology). Neither is covered by the old refutation.
findings.readingChosen: The implementer chose reading (ii), aid in kind is what a STRANGER is handed. The pool's state supports reading (i), aid in kind is what ANYONE here is handed, with the stranger as witness rather than recipient class: V2 FACE 2 has the ask made out loud in front of the neighbours, V2 FACE 4 has households giving toward a burying, the V1 spine has the households making up the difference. Nothing in the pool makes visitors the recipients. The fix keeps reading (i) and still puts the speaker in his own sentence for 42d.
findings.proposedFix: What is put into a hand here is goods and not coin, a stranger says, and no apology comes with the sack he is handed.

findings.was: 9 faces re-cut
findings.now: 0 new sentence shapes introduced
findings.why: Every face in the pool, before and after, is a role says a fact: 10 of 10 in variant 1, 9 of 9 in variant 2, 8 of 8 in variant 3. The brief names five other lawful shapes (someone FOUND something, someone DOES something, two people DISAGREE, nobody HAS DONE something, the bare fact the engine holds) and the cut used none. V2 FACE 5 made it worse by one, converting the pool's only fact-first line ("The bar coming down is heard at the far doors, by the account of those who hold the way through") into leading attribution ("Those who hold the way through say..."). The two [stranger] faces are the natural carriers for the FOUND shape, and V1 FACE 4 and V1 FACE 7 already end on a nobody-has-done sentence that could lead instead.
findings.proposedFix: V1 FACE 3 in the FOUND shape, same claim: A stranger found every pail at the water cut with a household's own mark, and the pail he is handed is the one without.

findings.was: The soldiers say the place says plainly what it wants of them, and the people here ask them straight out to put a shoulder to a load.
findings.now: The soldiers say the place says plainly what it wants of them. The people here ask them straight out to put a shoulder to a load.
findings.why: The split was made without running the 42a test, and the test points at the FIRST sentence, not the second. Delete sentence two and the face loses the only fact it has (what is wanted: a shoulder to a load). Delete sentence one and nothing is lost, because "the place says plainly what it wants of them" is the abstract version of the concrete sentence that follows - the writer telling the reader what to make of the fact, which under 42 must be gone. The first sentence is also 42b-empty on its own: the manner of asking measures nothing.
findings.proposedFix: The soldiers say the people here ask them straight out to put a shoulder to a load.

findings.was: The pails at the water each carry a household's own mark, a stranger says, and a visitor is handed the unmarked pail.
findings.now: The pails at the water each carry a household's own mark, a stranger says, and he was handed the unmarked one.
findings.why: A standing practice (a visitor IS handed the unmarked pail) became one past event (he WAS handed it): a change of tense and of habitual to one-off. It narrows rather than contradicts, and the definite article in "the unmarked one" still implies a designated visitor pail, so the old refutation still covers what is asserted and nothing new needs refuting. But the face now reports an anecdote where it reported an arrangement, and the arrangement was the informative half. The 42d gain (the speaker in his own sentence) can be kept without that loss.
findings.proposedFix: The pails at the water each carry a household's own mark, a stranger says, and the unmarked one is the pail he is handed.

findings.was: At the tavern they say the turn comes round to the same backs and never as far as the next roof.
findings.now: At the tavern the same backs say the turn comes round to them and never as far as the next roof.
findings.why: The claim does not move and the disagreement with FACE 5 is intact and sharper (the elders who set the turn against the households who bear it), so this is a good 42d edit. Two residues: the speaker narrowed from the tavern generally to the burdened households specifically, which is an assertion about who is talking that the source tag alone does not carry; and "the same backs" now stands as a grammatical subject with no antecedent, with backs doing the speaking, so a metonym that read naturally as an object reads oddly as a speaker.
findings.proposedFix: At the tavern the households that turn out say the turn comes round to them and never as far as the next roof.

untouchedFacesFailingTheStandard.text: Everyone here has seen who turns out when something is wanted, and takes it that the same people would turn out for anything worse.
untouchedFacesFailingTheStandard.whichRule: 42 - the trailing clause carries no fact. It reports the conclusion the reader was meant to draw from the first clause, and draws it about something that has not happened. Delete it and no fact is missing.
untouchedFacesFailingTheStandard.proposedFix: Everyone here has seen who turns out when something is wanted. Nothing worse than that has been asked of them.

untouchedFacesFailingTheStandard.text: At the market they say the place takes from whoever can be found, and there is nothing easier to find than a stall.
untouchedFacesFailingTheStandard.whichRule: 42 - "there is nothing easier to find than a stall" is a comparative generalisation whose only job is to explain why the first clause lands on the stallholders. It is the writer telling the reader what to make of the fact.
untouchedFacesFailingTheStandard.proposedFix: At the market they say the place takes from whoever can be found, and the stalls are what it finds.

untouchedFacesFailingTheStandard.text: The shortfall comes off the stalls, they say at the market, and the argument comes from behind every stall.
untouchedFacesFailingTheStandard.whichRule: 42b - "the argument comes from behind every stall" names no disagreement, which is the rule's own worked example (the town argues about this). Two readings fit: stallholders against the collectors, or stallholders against each other over who was asked for less. The line commits to neither.
untouchedFacesFailingTheStandard.proposedFix: The shortfall comes off the stalls, they say at the market, and every stallholder says the stall beside his was asked for less. NOTE: this is a 42b sharpening and is NOT covered by the old refutation - it must be refuted before landing. Reading chosen: stallholder against stallholder, because the pool's state is repeatedly that the burden falls on the same people and the others can be named (V1 FACE 6, V3 FACE 4).

untouchedFacesFailingTheStandard.text: The elders say the turn comes round to everyone who can spare a back.
untouchedFacesFailingTheStandard.whichRule: 42d - the elders are nowhere in their own sentence. From the line alone a reader can state the fact but cannot name what the elders stand to gain or lose, because nothing in the fact is theirs. The owner's models work because the speaker's own thing is in the fact (the hall's purse, the priest's sick house).
untouchedFacesFailingTheStandard.proposedFix: The elders say the turn they set comes round to everyone who can spare a back.

untouchedFacesFailingTheStandard.text: The elders hold that an ask is made out loud here and in front of the neighbours. A refusal is heard by the same ears.
untouchedFacesFailingTheStandard.whichRule: 42d - same defect as V1 FACE 5. The public ask is not the elders' own business on the face of the line, so no stake is drawable from the line alone.
untouchedFacesFailingTheStandard.proposedFix: The elders hold that an ask is made out loud here, in front of them and in front of the neighbours. A refusal is heard by the same ears.

untouchedFacesFailingTheStandard.text: The elders hold that a household with nothing else to spare still finds what it takes to put its own in the ground.
untouchedFacesFailingTheStandard.whichRule: 42d - the third elders face with no stake in its own sentence. The fact is entirely about the households; the elders only report it.
untouchedFacesFailingTheStandard.proposedFix: The elders say they have never known a household fail to find what it takes to put its own in the ground.

untouchedFacesFailingTheStandard.text: Those who keep the ground say a household gives toward a burying whatever it has. What is put in is remembered by the neighbours better than any count.
untouchedFacesFailingTheStandard.whichRule: 42a and 42 - "better than any count" is an evaluative comparative, not a fact, and it buries the fact it stands on (that nothing is written down). What survives is the neighbours remembering, which is a real second fact and earns its sentence.
untouchedFacesFailingTheStandard.proposedFix: Those who keep the ground say a household gives toward a burying whatever it has. The neighbours remember what each one put in.

leastSure: V1 FACE 6 NOW: 'At the tavern the same backs say the turn comes round to them and never as far as the next roof.' - I read the speaker-narrowing as the 42d fix it was clearly meant to be rather than a claim move, but a stricter chair could call naming the burdened households as the speakers an assertion the source tag does not license.

V1 FACE 3 NOW: '...and he was handed the unmarked one.' - I graded this a narrowing the old refutation still covers rather than a blocking move, because the definite article keeps the standing arrangement in view; on the parent's literal habitual-to-one-off test it would be blocking.

V2 FACE 8 NOW: 'One of the watch says the same corners get stood in whether the purse is settled or not. The round ends where it starts, at the water.' - the split is lawful under 42a because the second sentence adds a fact, but the two facts are unrelated to each other, which strains 42's one fact, one speaker in a way the comma version hid rather than caused.
